p.title: v59.97 the browser-data pin integrity check fetches its pinned commit instead of skipping in shallow CI checkouts
p.symptom: In CI the workspace contracts shard checks out at depth 1, so checkPinIntegrity found the pinned public-data commit absent and silently skipped the tree-vs-manifest and ancestry checks on every run; a manifest missing a deployed file or a pin outside main's history passed CI.
p.root_cause: scripts/browser-data-fixture.mjs only compared the pinned tree and ancestry when the commit already existed locally and reported 'absent' without a word otherwise.
p.fix: When the pin is absent and an origin remote exists, checkPinIntegrity fetches it once (git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin <sha>, no blob filter) and runs the tree-vs-manifest comparison; a pin origin cannot serve is an integrity failure naming the pin. checkPinIntegrity and git() take a repo option so the check can run against another working copy. Limit: after a depth-1 fetch the ancestry check still cannot run (shallow history) and prints '[browser-data-fixture] SKIP ancestry: shallow history (pin <sha12>)' instead of passing silently. Without an origin remote the absent pin keeps today's quiet skip.
p.violated_rule: A gate that cannot run its check must say so, not pass silently.
p.prevention: scripts/ci-browser-data-fixture-check.mjs v59.97 cases build a temporary remote and a depth-1 clone: the absent pin is fetched and matches, a manifest file missing from the pinned tree fails, and a pin the remote does not have fails with the sha named.
p.verification: node scripts/ci-browser-data-fixture-check.mjs exit 0; the three v59.97 cases fail with the old browser-data-fixture.mjs.

changelog: **Pin integrity runs in CI ({P}):** the browser-data pin check fetches its pinned commit in a shallow checkout and compares the tree with the manifest instead of skipping; ancestry prints a labelled shallow-history SKIP.
note: v59.97: pin integrity fetches the pin in shallow CI
